analysis_steps.goal: Measure dust disk size and flux

method.value: Gaussian model fit to continuum visibilities; cross-check with 1D Gaussian cuts deconvolved from beam

evidence.quote: Assuming a Gaussian model for the disk, we fitted for the disk size and its flux in the uv visibility plane.

assumptions.value: geometrically thin disk for inclination lower limit

evidence.quote: a lower limit on inclination angle from the line of sight of $i {\sim}30^{\circ}-35^{\circ}$ is found assuming a geometrically thin disk

validation.value: 1D Gaussian fits consistent with uv fit

evidence.quote: provides the disk FWHMs fully consistent with the measured disk size from the uv visibility fit

method.value: Optically thin 9 mm formula M=D^2F/(B(T)kappa), rescaled with T=100 K and Ossenkopf & Henning opacity

evidence.quote: The higher dust disk temperature of 100 K revealed by our observations reduces the mass to 0.08 $M_\odot$.

assumptions.value: dust T=100 K; aggregates without ice mantles, coagulation at >=1e8 cm-3 raises kappa by 6.5

evidence.quote: Using the corresponding model in (cite: Ossenkopf1994) increases $\kappa_\nu$ by a factor 6.5, decreasing the disk mass further to 0.01$M_\odot$.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit envelope infall/rotation to get stellar mass and angular momentum

method.value: Ballistic rotating-infalling envelope model compared to H13CO+ PV diagram perpendicular to jet

evidence.quote: well reproduced by a ballistic model of rotating and infalling flattened envelope
considering inclination angles ${\sim}30^\circ-44^\circ$
We find that the morphology of the brightest features in the observed P-V diagrams match well with the thin shell model.

validation.value: compared with Gaudel et al. 2020 l_env

evidence.quote: We checked that their measured $V(R)$ agree very well with the brightest "branches" of our PV cut in H$^{13}$CO$^+$.

method.value: L_acc = G M Mdot / R_star with L=9 Lsun, R=3 Rsun

evidence.quote: taking the appropriate stellar radius for an accreting protostar of this mass, $R_{\star}=3$ R$_{\odot}$ ((cite: Stahler1988))
assuming that the bolometric luminosity is dominated by the accretion luminosity

analysis_steps.goal: Retrieve outflow shape and kinematics from transverse PV

method.value: Thin axisymmetric rotating shell; measure max projected radii and velocities at z_proj=30-120 au, derive r(z), v_phi, v_z; model PV overlay with conical shape, linear v_z, constant v_phi=3.5 km/s

evidence.quote: Our model assumes a thin, axisymmetric rotating shell of gas to retrieve the flow shape $r(z)$, $v_{\phi}$ (rotational velocity), and $v_z$ (velocity along the axis).
we find $v_r$ by assuming that the poloidal velocity is tangential to the flow shape
we played with the various parameters to find the best-fit ring-like structure for the P-V diagrams

validation.value: black curves from the model compared to PV diagrams

evidence.quote: We find that the morphology of the brightest features in the observed P-V diagrams match well with the thin shell model.

analysis_steps.goal: Wind launching radius and lever arm

method.value: Anderson relation with measured r v_phi and v_tot for M*=0.3, 0.5 Msun; lambda_phi from r v_phi v_tot/GM = lambda sqrt(2 lambda-3)

evidence.quote: (rv_{\phi} \times v_{\rm tot})/GM_\star = \lambda_\phi \sqrt{2\lambda_\phi -3}.

assumptions.value: cold, steady, axisymmetric MHD wind, gravity neglected

evidence.quote: valid at any point in a cold, steady, axisymmetric MHD disk wind where gravitational potential can be neglected

validation.value: including gravity changes r0 by ~1-5 au

evidence.quote: would only affect the launching radius by ${\sim}1-5$ au

findings_qualitative.value: CH3OH and H13CN emission shows a central hole attributed to continuum over-subtraction of optically thick dust.

evidence.quote: Therefore, continuum over-subtraction is likely causing this hole in methanol emission.

findings_qualitative.value: H13CN PV cuts show nested onion-like velocity structure and ring at 120 au.

evidence.quote: suggestive of an "onion-like" nested velocity structure inside the low-velocity rotating flow

claims.hypothesis: CH3OH and H13CN trace a rotating MHD disk wind
claims.experiment: Transverse PV cuts and thin-shell model of the redshifted outflow
claims.result: Rotation signatures, conical shell with base ~19 au, r0~10 au
claims.finding: Suggestive evidence for MHD disk wind; first in H13CN and CH3OH

evidence.quote: This is the first detection of an MHD disk wind candidate in H$^{13}$CN and CH$_3$OH.

claims.hypothesis: The wind can drive disk accretion
claims.experiment: Mass-loss rate from H13CN vs accretion rate and f_M
claims.result: Mdot_DW total ~2.5-4 times accretion rate; f_M~4
claims.finding: Wind could carry enough angular momentum

evidence.quote: suggests that the rotating wind could carry enough angular momentum to drive disk accretion

claims.hypothesis: Central mass and centrifugal radius of the system
claims.result: M=0.4±0.1 Msun, Rb~24 au matching disk
claims.finding: centrifugal radius similar to dust disk radius

evidence.quote: indicate a central mass of $0.4\pm 0.1$ M$_\odot$ and a centrifugal radius similar to the dust disk radius

evidence.quote: the new ALMA observations presented here are the first able to resolve the base of the outflow in this object
